later_events.mechanism: statutory_repeal_of_code_approval_and_enforcement_provisions; later event of the approving order, not an end of this exhausted denial

clauses.reason: The sole operative paragraph says: "do order that the application for exemption by the above named applicants, be and it is hereby denied". A denial of an application for exemption commands nothing after it issues; its command is exhausted by performance on the date it is signed, September 18, 1933 (the order's date, confirmed against the held text and the mirror page record), because it leaves the applicants where the code puts them. The applicants' continuing obligation is the code's own operation, which the approving order governs and which ended with the repeal on June 14, 1935 under section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 ("All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"); that repeal is recorded as a later event, not as the end of this clause. The order contains no stay or exception, so there is no separate clause. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization of the section 3 delegation, not an end date for this order.

research_rationale:
EO 6296 (1933-09-18, Franklin D. Roosevelt), read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (registered grade mirror_transcription, not an original; 1540 characters). Identity: the census register lists it as 'Executive Order 6296—In the Matter of the Application of Gem-Dandy Garter Company for Certain Exemptions from the Corset and Brassiere Code' dated 1933-09-18; the WPA 1944 list has '1933 Sept 18 p.540: Application of the Gem-Dandy Garter Co. for certain exemptions from the Code of Fair Competition for the Corset and Bras siereIndustry denied. I NRA Codes 732.'. Page check: the mirror page record with the same source sha256 is headed 'Executive Order 6296—In the Matter of the Application of Gem-Dandy Garter Company for Certain Exemptions from the Corset and Brassiere Code', dated 1933-09-18, from a common-crawl capture of 2025-11-14T00:40:44Z, and its text_sha256 equals the held text's; the heading names this order's number and the date and subject agree with the text. The order recites that the Corset and Brassiere Industry code had been approved, that hearings were granted under the President's July 15, 1933 order to applicants who sought a wage differential for the southern section of the industry, and that "no case of injustice and extreme hardship requiring special treatment has been made out by the above applicants". Single operative command: "do order that the application for exemption by the above named applicants, be and it is hereby denied". A denial of an application commands nothing after it issues; under the shared analysis it is exhausted by performance on the date signed, September 18, 1933, with the S.J. Res. 113 repeal of June 14, 1935 as a later event. The applicants' continuing obligation after the denial was the code's own operation, governed by the approving order (EO 6248, held) and ended with the repeal; it is not a surviving command of this order.

savings.reason: The denial's effect is that the applicants remained subject to the Code of Fair Competition for the Corset and Brassiere Industry on its terms; that obligation arose from the approving order and the code, not from this order, and it ended with the section 2 repeal of S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935. Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before that date, including any liability of the applicants, are accrued effects; the general savings statute of the time (not a held source) preserved liabilities already incurred under a repealed statute. Section 5 of the Act exempted from the antitrust laws "any code, agreement, or license approved, prescribed, or issued and in effect under this title" and complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days after; the proviso in section 2 of the resolution says the exemption "shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder" of two kinds and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for past action. Nothing held continues the denial or the code after June 14, 1935.
